Let $T(t)$ denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter $t.$ Since we are given the curve $r(t)$ parametrized by the parameter $t$ (not the arc length $s$), we will use the following formula for the curvature:

$$
κ(t)=\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{tan}⁡t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{tan}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{{sec}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\operatorname{sec}⁡t\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡t}⟨\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate ${T}^{′}(t)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}κ(t) & =\frac{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}=\frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡t}=\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Let T(t) denote the unit tangent to the given curve as a function of the parameter t. Since we are given the curve r(t) parametrized by the parameter t (not the arc length s), we will use the following formula for the curvature: κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖

Now, we calculate r′(t) and find its magnitude: r′(t)=⟨ddt(−ln⁡(cos⁡t)),ddt(t)⟩=⟨tan⁡t,1⟩‖r′(t)‖=(tan⁡t)2+12=tan2⁡t+1=sec2⁡t=sec⁡t

Hence, the corresponding unit tangent vector is T(t)=r′(t)‖r′(t)‖=1sec⁡t⟨tan⁡t,1⟩=⟨sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩.

Next, we calculate T′(t) and find its magnitude: T′(t)=⟨ddt(sin⁡t),ddt(cos⁡t)⟩=⟨cos⁡t,−sin⁡t⟩‖T′(t)‖=(cos⁡t)2+(−sin⁡t)2=cos2⁡t+sin2⁡t=1

Finally, the curvature is κ(t)=‖T′(t)‖‖r′(t)‖=1sec⁡t=cos⁡t.
